Article Title: Wife pours hot water on husband following a quarrel
Article Text:
Nagpur:





A 26-year-old woman allegedly poured hot water on her husband on Thursday following a quarrel at their home in Kawtha village under Koradi police station limits.As per police, the victim, Nilesh Tate, a 36-year-old milk seller, and his wife Karishma , frequently quarrelled over minor domestic issues. The situation took a violent turn on Thursday night when he returned home after distributing milk. Nilesh was freshening up when Karishma allegedly brought a steel bucket filled with hot water and poured it on him from the front.The hot water caused burns to his throat, chest, neck, back and both the hands. He suffered serious injuries and was rushed to a medical facility for treatment. Following the incident, Nilesh lodged a complaint against his wife. Based on his statement, police registered a case against his wife Karishma.Police are investigating the incident to establish the circumstances that led to the alleged attack. Details about the woman’s response to the allegations were not immediately available.
Article Summary: Nilesh Tate, a 36-year-old milk seller, and his wife Karishma frequently quarrelled over minor domestic issues. The situation took a violent turn on Thursday night when he returned home after distributing milk. Nilesh was freshening up when his wife allegedly brought a steel bucket filled with hot water and poured it on him.

Article Title: Jalgaon police register case against road construction firm, engineer for death of 12-year-old in accident
Article Text:
Nashik:





Police have filed a case against a road construction company owner, a road engineer and a truck driver after a 12-year-old boy was killed and his father was seriously injured in an accident on Humbardi-Faizpur road in Jalgaon on Friday.Faizpur police identified the deceased boy as Lalit Kaviraj Chavan, a native of Burhanpur district in Madhya Pradesh who was residing in Anjala village in Yaval taluka. His father, Kaviraj, suffered serious injuries and is undergoing treatment.According to police, the father and son were travelling on a motorcycle from Faizpur towards Anjala around 7pm when a truck allegedly coming from the wrong side of the road crashed into their vehicle. The driver fled the spot without informing authorities or helping the victims. Lalit died from his injuries, while the motorcycle was badly damaged.Based on a complaint lodged by the injured man’s brother-in-law, police registered a case under Section 106(1) (causing death by negligence) and other relevant provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).The complaint alleged that ongoing road construction work was being carried out without adequate safety measures, warning signs or precautions, creating a hazardous situation that contributed to the fatal accident.
Article Summary: A 12-year-old boy was killed and his father was seriously injured in an accident on Humbardi-Faizpur road in Jalgaon on Friday. Police have filed a case against a road construction company owner, a road engineer and a truck driver. The complaint alleged that ongoing road construction work was being carried out without adequate safety measures.

Article Title: Jalgaon police dispose of seized drugs worth Rs 65.7 crore
Article Text:
Disposal of Drugs by Jalgaon police

Nashik





: The Jalgaon police have disposed of narcotics worth Rs65.7 crore seized during two separate raids in the district.The contraband was transported from Jalgaon to M/s Maharashtra Enviro Power Ltd. at MIDC Ranjangaon in the Shirur taluka of Pune district on Friday. The transit took place under heavy police security, and the entire disposal process was video-recorded to maintain complete legal transparency.In July last year, the Jalgaon police seized over 43 kg of amphetamine worth Rs64.5 crore. The drugs were being transported in a car from Delhi to Bengaluru. The driver, who already had a case registered against him in Bengaluru approximately six years ago, was arrested. Acting on a tip-off about the drug smuggling operation, the Jalgaon police laid a trap, and the highway police intercepted the vehicle at Kannad Ghat.The Dhule rural police were called in for assistance and subsequently sought help from the forensic science department, which confirmed the substance was amphetamine. Following the confirmation, the car and contraband were seized, the driver was arrested, and a case was registered with the Chalisgaon rural police.Meanwhile, 884 grams of methaqualone were destroyed from a separate case registered with the Bhusawal Bazarpeth police station in 2024.The disposal of the drugs was carried out under the guidance of Jalgaon superintendent of police (SP) Srikant Dhivare.Officials stated that the destruction of seized narcotics is executed in accordance with Section 52-A of the NDPS Act, 1985, and its applicable rules. This protocol is strictly followed to prevent seized contraband from being stolen, resold illicitly, or re-entering the illegal market. The drugs are destroyed using controlled, high temperatures in an industrial furnace, ensuring the process causes no adverse effects on the air, water, or general environment.
Article Summary: The contraband was transported from Jalgaon to M/s Maharashtra Enviro Power Ltd. at MIDC Ranjangaon in the Shirur taluka of Pune district on Friday. The entire disposal process was video-recorded to maintain complete legal transparency. The drugs are destroyed using controlled, high temperatures in an industrial furnace.

Article Title: Two siblings held on charge of stabbing fabrication worker to death after row over damaged shoes in bikes’ collision in Ahilyanagar
Article Text:
The arrested siblings have been remanded in police custody till Oct 12

Nashik:





Two siblings were arrested from Mumbai on Thursday for allegedly stabbing to death a 55-year-old fabrication worker as shoes of one of them was damaged after their motorcycle brushed the victim’s two-wheeler on Balikashram Road in Ahilyanagar on Wednesday evening.The deceased fabrication worker was identified as Ravindra Rambhau Chavan (55), a resident of Bhingardive Mala at Bhutkarwadi in Savedi, Ahilyanagar. The arrested siblings, Suraj Ravi Sonawane and Prem alias Sonulya Ravi Sonawane from Siddharthnagar in Ahilyanagar, were produced before a court and remanded in police custody till Oct 12.Tofkhana police registered a case of murder against Suraj and Sonulya under relevant sections of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, and the Arms Act, 1959, based on a complaint filed by the victim’s son, Manthan Ravindra Chavan (25).Police said the victim, Ravindra, was riding the motorcycle around 5pm on Wednesday with an acquaintance, Mikhail Shankar Bhakare. Their two-wheeler slightly sideswiped the motorcycle of the accused. The shoes of one of the riders of the other motorcycle was damaged in the minor collision and an argument broke out over it.Inspector Balaji Vaidya of Tofkhana police said the accused duo allegedly attacked Ravindra with sharp weapons in the course of the altercation and inflicted severe injuries on his back and left arm. Bhakare immediately alerted the victim’s family about the latter’s injury over the phone. Ravindra was rushed to Civil Hospital in Ahilyanagar, where attending doctors declared him dead on arrival.
Article Summary: The deceased fabrication worker was identified as Ravindra Rambhau Chavan (55), a resident of Bhingardive Mala at Bhutkarwadi in Savedi, Ahilyanagar. The arrested siblings, Suraj Ravi Sonawane and Prem alias Sonulya RaviSonawane, were produced before a court and remanded in police custody till Oct 12.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi accuses Modi, Shah and Doval of ‘attacking youth’, turning Delhi into prison
Article Text:
Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi participates in ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ (Students’ Voices) event at Island Grounds in Chennai, on Saturday





Chennai: Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi , Union home minister Amit Shah and National Security Adviser Ajit Doval had “attacked the youth” of India.Speaking to reporters at Chennai airport, Gandhi accused the trio of turning Delhi into a “prison” and unleashing “BJP goondas” against young protesters. “No matter what they do, the trap is closing in on them. There is no escape because they have conspired against the people, democracy and the Constitution of this country. The entire opposition and the youth are slowly squeezing the space out,” he said.Gandhi also alleged that Modi, Shah and Gyanesh Kumar had “destroyed democracy” and “attacked the heart and soul of the country”. “The youth of this country, boys and girls who have been attacked in Delhi today, and the entire opposition will get justice,” he said. “Mark my words.”
Article Summary: Gandhi accused the trio of turning Delhi into a ‘prison’ and unleashing ‘BJP goondas’ against young protesters. “No matter what they do, the trap is closing in on them. There is no escape because they have conspired against the people, democracy and the Constitution of this country,” he said.

Article Title: TVK’s P Sathyabama wins Dharapuram byelection; Vijay party's Maragatham Kumaravel extends her lead in Madurantakam
Article Text:
TVK candidate P Sathyabama with party president and Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay





COIMBATORE/CHENNAI: TVK candidate P Sathyabama on Friday won the Dharapuram byelection by a margin of 9,471 votes, securing 66,841 votes.DMK candidate S Suganya came second with 57,370 votes, while AIADMK's K Banumathi secured 45,280 votes.The bypoll was necessitated after Sathyabama, who had won Dharapuram seat as an AIADMK candidate in the April assembly election, resigned as MLAs and joined the ruling TVK.Meanwhile, at the of 16th round of counting of votes in Madurantakam , TVK candidate Maragatham Kumaravel secured 63,391 votes, extending her lead over DMK candidate I Paranthaman (46,086 votes) to 17,305 votes. AIADMK candidate Kanitha Sampath remained in third place with 41,133 votes.Maragatham, who had won the Madurantakam seat as an AIADMK candidate in the last assembly election, resigned as MLAs and joined the ruling TVK, like Sathyabama.Polling was held in Dharapuram and Madurantakam on Oct 6.
Article Summary: TVK candidate P Sathyabama on Friday won the Dharapuram byelection by a margin of 9,471 votes, securing 66,841 votes. DMK candidate S Suganya came second with 57,370 votes, while AIADMK's K Banumathi secured 45,280 votes.

Article Title: Dharapuram bypoll: EVMs, VVPATs secured under two-tier armed cover, 24x7 CCTV surveillance
Article Text:
Representative image





TIRUPUR: Electronic voting machines (EVMs) and voter verifiable paper audit trail (VVPAT) units used for the Dharapuram assembly byelection in Tirupur district have been placed in a strong room under two-tier armed security and round-the-clock CCTV surveillance, officials said.After the completion of polling on Oct 6, the EVMs and VVPAT units were brought to the counting centre located at LRG Govt Women’s Arts College in the district.District election officer and collector Dr Manish Narnaware and election general observer Chinmay Pundlikrao Gotmare, IAS, on Wednesday supervised the placement of machines into the strong room in the presence of candidates and their agents. The strong room was sealed thereafter, with the participation of superintendent of police Srishti Singh, IPS, deputy commissioner of police Akash Joshi, IPS, and Dharapuram revenue divisional officer A Felix Raja.Narnaware said the strong room would be opened on Oct 9 -- the counting day -- in the presence of candidates or their representatives and the central observer, under videography.District election authorities said the strong room was being protected with armed security personnel in a two-tier arrangement, with continuous monitoring through CCTV cameras.To ensure uninterrupted supervision of CCTV feeds, three officers of deputy collector rank have been deployed daily at the district level, while separate monitoring officers have been appointed for the assembly constituency.The monitoring will continue until the counting day on Oct 9.Authorities said all contesting candidates have been informed in writing about appointing representatives to observe the security arrangements, with permission granted for such representatives to stay outside the inner security cordon.Polling was held at 320 booths in the constituency. There are 2,23,306 registered voters, and 1,79,214 votes were cast, recording a turnout of 80.25%.
Article Summary: Electronic voting machines used for Dharapuram assembly byelection in Tirupur district. EVMs and VVPAT units placed in strong room under two-tier armed security and round-the-clock CCTV surveillance. The monitoring will continue until the counting day on Oct 9.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.
